project_overview: This Vue.js application appears to manage student data and exam-related processes, likely within an educational domain. The codebase demonstrates a modular structure with several Vue components dedicated to specific features such as exam submissions, results, and user profiles. The interconnectedness, indicated by the dependency graph, suggests a complex system with potential challenges related to maintainability and scalability. The presence of multiple ‘iLike’ components suggests personalized learning features.

macro_trends.title: Potential Prop Drilling and High-Level Vue Dependence
macro_trends.description: Several components (e.g., ApplicationServices, ResultPage) directly depend on other Vue components (e.g., SelectedApplicationService, Transactions). This suggests potential prop drilling – passing data through multiple layers unnecessarily – and might increase the complexity of managing state across the application.  Further investigation into the data flow is warranted.

macro_trends.title: Centralized Route Navigation
macro_trends.description: A significant number of Router push actions are centralized, potentially leading to tight coupling between components. This could hinder independent development and testing.

key_workflows.name: Exam Submission Workflow
key_workflows.description: This workflow begins with the user filling out the ExamFormSubmission component and then potentially validating/processing data through Transactions before finally displaying the ResultPage. The specific details regarding the backend processing are unknown. The Router pushes guide the user through this process.

key_workflows.name: User Profile Management
key_workflows.description: This workflow centers around updating user details (e.g., through addEducationalDetails or updatePersonalDetails). Router pushes navigate the user between different profile sections, and potential concerns exist around data consistency and potential state management vulnerabilities.
